summary:
Work Design Magazine podcast show notes for an episode of "What the F* is Happening to the Office?" hosted by Bob Fox, featuring Celeste Tell, workplace strategist, circular economy advocate and co-founder of Epicycled.

The central argument: in an era of constant organizational change, designing a workplace for a single fixed outcome is designing for failure. Tell proposes treating the workplace as a "kit of parts," analogized to original Lego bricks rather than themed Lego sets, so space can be reconfigured repeatedly without a full rip-out and rebuild.

Discussion points listed in the show notes include: why architects and contractors disengage on day one, leaving owners holding space that no longer fits; why landfill economics are the real obstacle to circularity in workplace design; how the auto industry mastered extended producer responsibility while office design has not; and what it would look like to genuinely design a workplace for a 50-year lease.

The intended audience is corporate real estate, architecture, workplace strategy and facilities professionals, particularly those who have seen a functional, highly customized space scraped after organizational change.

The item is promotional show notes rather than a reported article, so it contains no statistics, survey data or named customer examples. It does not address desk booking, visitor management, hybrid attendance policy or workplace analytics tooling. Credits: created and directed by Bob Fox, produced by Work Design Studios.
